caption: Distance is its own line item out here. Is anyone else's fuel bill basically a second rent?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R24 000
p/m salary
Living in Springbok
slides.body:
Male, 48
Divorced, kids grown and living in Cape Town
Job: Water technician, local municipality
Net salary: R24 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.includes: 2 bed house, bought after the divorce
slides.body: Small house, but it's mine and nobody else's name is on it.

slides.title: Bakkie instalment
slides.includes: Double cab, does 40 000km a year on service routes
slides.body: The municipality doesn't pay per kilometre, so half of this is me subsidising the job.

slides.title: Fuel
slides.includes: Nearest big town is two hours away, and so is everything else
slides.body: People in the city spend this on rent. Out here it's just the cost of distance.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: One supermarket in town, no competition to keep prices down
slides.body: I pay city prices in a town with a fraction of the choice.

slides.title: Phone & data
slides.includes: Extra data because the signal drops on half my routes
slides.body: I pay more to be reachable out here than I did living in a city.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, funeral policy, insurance, electricity & water, support to his mother, a flight to see his kids twice a year
slides.body: The flights are the one I resent least. Everything else on this list I'd cut if I could.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R24 000. Out here that's not bad, until the bakkie needs new tyres.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction, fuel included.

Seeing the distance costs added up in one number was the wake-up call.

No bank login needed.
